#my code chunk to import and plot data 
```{r}
#import phenotypes data into an R object dataframe
phenotypes_df <- read.csv("../../common-disease-genomics-data/phenotypes.csv")

#check
#make a plot and add it to your R environment as an object called "myplot"
myplot <- ggplot(phenotypes_df, aes(x = bmi_kg_m2)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of BMI", x = "BMI", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

#you will need to change the "common-disease-genomics-data" part of the path to your data directory.
ggsave("../../test-data/BMI_histogram.png", plot = myplot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```



#importing genotype data
```{r}
#import synthetic genotype data into an R object dataframe
genotypes_df <- read.csv("../../common-disease-genomics-data/genotypes.csv")

```


#Analyse my genotype and indication pair in the synthetic data
```{r}
#select phenotype
my_indication <- select(phenotypes_df, c(subject_id, age_years, sex, ldl_mg_dl))

#select genotype
my_genotype <- select(genotypes_df, c(subject_id, PCSK9_rs11591147))

#join
my_gene_indication_pair <- left_join(my_indication, my_genotype, by="subject_id")

#rename your columns to something easier
my_gene_indication_pair <- my_gene_indication_pair %>% rename(LDL = "ldl_mg_dl", PCSK9_genotype ="PCSK9_rs11591147", age = "age_years")

#summarise the data subset by the three PCSK9 genotypes.
my_gene_indication_pair %>%
  group_by(PCSK9_genotype) %>%
  summarise(across(c(age, LDL), list(mean = mean)))

summary <- my_gene_indication_pair %>%
  group_by(PCSK9_genotype) %>%
  summarise(across(c(age, LDL), list(mean = mean)))

#HERE HERE HERE HERE 
summary <- my_gene_indication_pair %>%
  group_by(PCSK9_genotype) %>%
  summarise(across(c(age, LDL), list(mean = mean, n = sum, sd = sd)))

#perform some basic regression analyses
model_crude <- lm(LDL ~ PCSK9_genotype, data = my_gene_indication_pair)
summary(model_crude)
#now adjust for sex and age to reduce the spread or "variance" in the data.






```






#This table describes the basic features of a synthetic dataset that includes phenotypes and genotypes generated by Claude. The relationship between genotypes and phenotypes is representative
```{r}
#calculate basic descriptive data and output to a table
#first for continuous data
age_stats <- summary(phenotypes_df$age_years)
bmi_stats <- summary(phenotypes_df$bmi_kg_m2)


continuous_stats <- rbind(age_stats, bmi_stats)
print(continuous_stats)


#this is Claude's suggestion on how to make the basic summary data look more professional.
#note that Claude uses "df" instead of the name of our df which is "phenotypes_df* and "age* instead of "age_years"
#so lets modify our dataframe names so that we do not need to modify Claude's code. 

df <- phenotypes_df %>% rename(age = "age_years", bmi = "bmi_kg_m2", disease1 = "cad_status", disease2 = "t2d_status")


#Claude code solution: 

# Summary stats
tbl <- rbind(
  "Age (years)"      = c(Mean=round(mean(df$age),1),   SD=round(sd(df$age),1),   "%"=""),
  "BMI (kg/m²)"     = c(Mean=round(mean(df$bmi),1),   SD=round(sd(df$bmi),1),   "%"=""),
  "Female sex"       = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$sex=="F")*100,1),"%")),
  "Hypertension"     = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$disease1)*100,1),"%")),
  "T2Diabetes"         = c(Mean="",                       SD="",                     "%"=paste0(round(mean(df$disease2)*100,1),"%"))
)

kable(tbl, caption="Table 1. Participant characteristics")



```



#code chunk to import GWAS summary stats and investigate specific chromosomes
```{r}
#import real GWAS data from my INDICATION and the chromosome that contains the gene that encodes the TARGET protein
CAD_chr9_df <- read.csv("../../common-disease-genomics-data/GWAS_coronary_artery_disease/chr_CAD9.csv")

#is the SNP used in the synthetic data present in the real GWAS data ?
CAD_chr9_mySNP_df <- CAD_chr9_df %>% filter(rsid == "rs10757278")

#filter on all variants in the gene and 100 kilo base pairs either side
#HERE HERE
#CAD_chr9_mygene_df <- CAD_chr9_df %>% filter(base_pair_location < )
#chr9:21,967,752-21,974,857




#now lets plot the effect of the key variant on the INDICATION, including the 95% confidence intervals (based on the standard error) using the ggplot2 function
# first calculate 95% CIs from the standard error
CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$ci_lower <- CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$beta - 1.96 * CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$standard_error
CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$ci_upper <- CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$beta + 1.96 * CAD_chr9_mySNP_df$standard_error

myplot <- ggplot(CAD_chr9_mySNP_df, aes(x = beta, y = reorder(rsid, beta))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Beta (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

print(myplot)
```
